# body right below. Why: Quarto rebuilds the author line of the title block on
# its own, and any Lua filter that tries to build it loses the superscripts and
# the correspondence line. Verified with Quarto 1.9.38 -> .docx.
# Affiliation numbering is manual, but it is explicit and comes out identical
# in .docx, .pdf and .html.
# The copyright holders in LICENSE-CODE and in the README come from this block.
author:
  - name: "First Author name^1,\\*^"
  - name: "Second Author name^2^"
keywords: [keyword 1, keyword 2, keyword 3]
date: today
date-format: long

```{r package-bibliography}
#| include: false
#| purl: false
# Writes the .bib entries of the packages in use, so they can be cited in
# Methods. It runs last, once they are all loaded. Pandoc reads packages.bib
# after knitr, so citations already work in this same pass.
#
# .packages() only sees what is ATTACHED during the render. Packages that
# prepared the data or the metadata (dataspice, readxl) ran in another session
# and would never get an entry, yet they deserve the citation as much as the
# rest. They are added by name; any that is not installed is skipped.
pkg_extra <- c("knitr", "quarto", "rmarkdown", "renv", "dataspice", "readxl",
               "easypaper")
pkg_extra <- pkg_extra[vapply(pkg_extra, requireNamespace, logical(1),
                              quietly = TRUE)]
knitr::write_bib(c(.packages(), pkg_extra),
                 here::here("references/packages.bib"))
```
